title: Box within Line-Numbered Prose

illustrates.quote: The length of box lines within line-numbered text adheres to the required two blank cells before line numbers.

blocks.text: gained, and write them out for publication. And he added:
blocks.features: End of running line-numbered prose, print line 80 (right-margin line-number column; facsimile image of a line-numbered manuscript page).

An indented quotation box drawn around print lines 81-82, opened with a top box line only; the box's own bottom edge is drawn as a jagged, torn-paper line beneath line 82 (confirmed against the PDF page image, p.187, footer 7-3), with line 83's row in the line-number gutter left blank (no text visible there). Read as the source figure being a deliberately cropped/partial illustration, consistent with the braille's own '444' continuation marker in place of a bottom box line. Matches 7.3.3.b: the braille top box line stops short (35 of 40 cells) to leave the required two blank cells before the line-number field.

blocks.text: "Never say ‘We learn’ so-and-so, or ‘It is reported,’ or ‘It is rumored,’ or ‘We understand’ so-and-so, but go to
blocks.features: Print lines 81-82 of the line-numbered quotation (line 81 wraps across two print lines in the source image; line 82 ends the excerpt, cut off by the box's own torn bottom edge after 'but go to'). The braille excerpt itself ends this same quotation with a '444' continuation marker rather than a bottom box line -- the quotation is evidently longer than what either the print image or the braille excerpt reproduces.

print.notes: Two-part print image: (1) a facsimile of ordinary line-numbered prose (line 80, unboxed) ending 'And he added:'; (2) immediately below/right, an indented box containing the start of a quotation (lines 81-82), whose print border is drawn torn off (no bottom line, no line-83 text) -- the source figure is itself a deliberately partial excerpt, not a complete page.
print.printFeatures: Photographic facsimile of a line-numbered manuscript page; the quotation box is a plain-ruled rectangle (top line only) inset within the shared right-margin line-number gutter used by both the running text and the box.

braille.notes: 7 lines (source .txt lines 5427-5433; fixed left margin of 8 characters stripped, U+2800 converted to space, trailing spaces stripped). Line 1: print line 80 ('gained, and write them out for publication. And he added:'), right-justified line-number code '#hj' (=80). Line 2: wrapped continuation of line 80 ('he added:'), no line-number code (same print line as line 1). Line 3: blank (a box is preceded by a blank line, 7.2.1). Line 4: the top box line, 35 dot-2356 '7' characters -- NOT the full 40-cell width; per 7.3.3.b it stops short to leave the required two blank cells before the line-number field (unlike Example 7-2's box lines, which run the full 40 cells because that example is not set within line-numbered text). No bottom box line appears in this excerpt. Line 5: print line 81, opening quotation mark and text, line-number code '#ha' (=81). Line 6: continuation of line 81's wrapped text, no line-number code. Line 7: print line 82, ending in a '444' continuation-omission marker, line-number code '#hb' (=82).

uncertain: Print line 83's row in the line-number gutter is visible but blank in the source page image -- the print box's own bottom border is drawn as a jagged, torn-paper line after line 82 rather than a normal ruled bottom edge. Read as the source figure being a deliberately partial/cropped illustration (consistent with the braille excerpt also truncating the same quotation with a '444' marker rather than a bottom box line), not as evidence that line 83 contained further boxed text that was simply omitted from transcription.

The BANA line-number encoding was decoded by the standard a=1..j=0 letter-for-digit convention (#hj=80, #ha=81, #hb=82); not cross-checked against a separate Special Symbols page in this reference copy.
resolution: braille.lines byte-identical between A and B. Print content and structure agree; wording differs only in how the box's own torn bottom edge is described (A: 'wavy/cut-off line'; B: 'hand-torn/frayed edge') -- both describe the same jagged torn-paper-style line, confirmed directly against the PDF page image (p.187, footer 7-3). Title uses the bare descriptive form ('Box within Line-Numbered Prose'), matching the section-4/8 gold precedent's own convention -- B's title field wrongly carried a literal 'Example 7-1:' prefix, not used. This box carries no title of its own (contrast Example 7-2's 'Forms of be'). BOTH runs transcribed the quotation's nested quotation marks as straight ASCII apostrophes ('We learn'); corrected to proper Unicode single quotation marks (‘We learn’) matching the print image's own typographic quotes -- confirmed by direct translate() experiment that only the curly form reproduces the expected braille's own nested-quote indicator (',8,we le>n,0'); the straight-apostrophe form translates as a plain apostrophe-word instead, which does not match. (This sample still mismatches Emboss's own output for unrelated reasons -- see standards-findings.md F-70/F-76.)
